description: Reproducing PROC REG with an OUTEST= parameter dataset: BY-group processing, exact column layout, RMSE from aliasing-aware degrees of freedom, and the -1 dependent-variable marker.

outest_layout.title: PROC REG OUTEST= writes one row per model with a fixed column layout and marks the response column with -1.
rule: OUTEST= produces a wide parameter dataset, one row per fitted model (per BY group).
Standard leading columns: any BY variables, then _MODEL_ (e.g. 'MODEL1'), _TYPE_ ('PARMS'), _DEPVAR_ (the response name), _RMSE_ (root mean squared error).
Then one column per regressor holding its estimated coefficient, plus 'Intercept' unless the model specifies NOINT.
The response variable also appears as its own column with the constant value -1 (SAS uses -1 to flag the dependent variable in OUTEST).
With a BY statement, process each group independently and preserve BY sort order in the output.
_RMSE_ = sqrt(SSE / df) where df = n_obs - model_rank; model_rank counts only non-aliased columns (see sas_singularity_rank).
pitfalls: Forgetting the -1 response column, or omitting Intercept handling under NOINT, breaks structural QC.
Computing df as n - p_nominal instead of n - rank overstates df when columns are aliased.
Rows with missing model variables are dropped listwise before fitting (match SAS).
